comment: Cross-implementation anchor for decisionOutcomeFromEvidence and decisionSummaryFromEvidence (kernel/src/evidence-decision.ts). The rules a second implementation must reproduce, written so it can be coded from this file without reading the TypeScript: (1) circuitBreaker.level >= 3 is `blocked`, checked FIRST — the loop was stopped by harness policy and calling that a `fail` would blame the app. (2) Otherwise an assertion present (key present and not null) decides `pass` when its `passed` is true, `fail` when false. (3) Otherwise a diagnosis present decides `NO_ANOMALY` -> pass, `INCONCLUSIVE` -> inconclusive, any T-class -> fail. (4) Otherwise `inconclusive`: nothing was asserted and nothing diagnosed is not a pass. (5) A pass is then downgraded — never upgraded — to `inconclusive` when attribution.contaminated is true or attribution.level is `weak`, because the engine itself refuses to attribute that result to this operation. Absent vs explicit-null for assertion/diagnosis are two shapes the engine really emits and must be treated the same way. The summary is a rendering of the same fields in this order, joined by '; ': 'assertion <property> passed|failed: expected <JSON>, actual <JSON>' when an assertion is present; 'diagnosis <class>: <report.anomaly>' when a diagnosis is present; 'circuitBreaker level <n> (<reason>)' when level > 0 (the parenthetical only when a reason is present); 'attribution <level>' plus ', contaminated' when contaminated. JSON values are rendered as JavaScript's JSON.stringify would (no insignificant whitespace, key order as the pack carries them). Longer than 2048 characters, keep the first 2045 and append '...'. Provenance: four cases are real packs read out of ~/.glasspane/evidence on 2026-10-08 (operationId recorded per case); four are derived by editing exactly one field of a recorded pack, stated in each case's `origin`, because the archived corpus never contains a failed assertion, a weak-or-contaminated pass, or a breaker at the policy limit — those rules can only be pinned by derivation, and a fixture that silently invented them would be unsourced. The `input` bytes are the archived files exactly as the engine wrote them, including a `schemaVersion` of `glasspane.evidence/0.1-draft` and a `pixelDiff` with no `bounds`. A consumer that reads evidence off disk therefore parses them through the read-side contract (`parseEvidencePackRead`), which is what folds the legacy version and tolerates the missing signal — the same path the GlassPane Harness ledger uses. The transcription itself reads only `attribution`, `assertion`, `diagnosis` and `circuitBreaker`, which are identical under both contracts; nothing here depends on version folding.
